This workflow runs only when the user invokes it. Claude must not start it
automatically.

## Invariants

- One authoritative owner per policy. Elsewhere use a routing pointer ("run
  workflow X", "see file Y") or a yes/no check-by-reference — never a reworded
  copy. Decision summaries appear only in CLAUDE.md § Architecture Defaults and
  `docs/technology-stack.md`.
- Keep each policy at its trigger: CLAUDE.md and `docs/technology-stack.md` only
  for planning-time policy; a flat path-scoped rule for constraints on files of
  an area; a workflow skill for procedure steps, stop conditions, and output
  shape. Do not promote content into CLAUDE.md to make loading easier, and do not
  demote planning-time policy to save tokens.
- Knowledge skills and private references hold technique only; they never own a
  must/must-not policy. A private reference is read only by its owning skill.
- Every instruction file starts with the one-line
  `> Owns: ... | Scope: ... | Loads: ...` header; every rule declares `paths`;
  `.claude/rules/` stays flat. CLAUDE.md imports only
  `docs/technology-stack.md`.
- Keep CLAUDE.md, `docs/technology-stack.md`, and skill descriptions compact;
  descriptions start with concrete triggers.
- Hooks are registered in exec form — `"command": "node"` with
  `"args": ["${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/<script>.mjs"]`, never a shell
  command string. The placeholder only locates the script; hooks derive the
  repository root they inspect from the hook input (`cwd`, or the edited file's
  location) and checkers from the current directory
  (`.claude/scripts/repo-root.mjs`). Hooks fail visibly and point messages at
  the owning file instead of restating policy. The dependency guard runs on
  PreToolUse, PostToolUse, and PostToolUseFailure for Bash and PowerShell, so a
  shell call that fails after changing a manifest is still checked. The
  PreToolUse guard also sets `"onFailure": "block"`, so a guard that cannot run
  blocks the tool call; advisory post-tool and Stop hooks do not.
- Product inputs (`SPECIFICATION.md`, `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md`) stay inputs; they do
  not carry instructions.

When the project uses Angular Material, use its components consistently for
common UI primitives where they satisfy the requirement. Do not add Angular
Material automatically to an existing project that has not chosen it, and do not
wrap every Material component in a custom abstraction without a concrete reason.

## API Client Generation

When OpenAPI client generation is adopted, treat generated code as generated,
keep it separate from handwritten feature logic, and regenerate it when the API
contract changes. Backend contract documentation: `swagger` skill.

## Testing

Test frontend behavior at the appropriate level: meaningful component behavior,
validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, complex
reactive state. Do not test Angular framework internals. E2E tests focus on a
small number of important user workflows unless the project requires broader
E2E coverage, and the same behavior is not duplicated at every test level. Use
the test runner configured in `package.json`.

Generate separate or clearly grouped OpenAPI descriptions for supported versions
when clients need them (`swagger` skill); the documented version must match
runtime routing and Controller metadata. Version changes do not override normal
HTTP semantics (`http-api` skill).

## Testing

When versions coexist, test meaningful differences: version routing,
version-specific response shape, a deprecated version still operational during
its support period, unsupported-version behavior, and shared Application
behavior staying consistent where intended. Do not duplicate identical tests
because two versions share Application behavior.

## Anti-Patterns

Avoid Minimal API version-group examples in a Controller-based project, creating
a new API version for every implementation change, and mixing URL, header, and
query versioning without a concrete reason.

## Verification

When API behavior changes:

2. verify response metadata;
3. start the API when the change affects startup/composition;
4. open the Development Swagger UI and confirm it loads;

Determine whether the failure comes from source code or the local toolchain

Use bounded iteration — several focused attempts, not an unlimited edit/build
loop. Stop and reassess when:

- the same root failure survives repeated, materially different fixes;
- fixes create increasing unrelated failures;
- the installed toolchain is incompatible;
- required external infrastructure is unavailable;
- package compatibility cannot be resolved safely;

`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), inspect the final repository tree,
and confirm the Development configuration is valid. Then run `verify`. Never
report successful scaffolding for a solution that does not build.

Investigate every newly failing relevant test; do not dismiss a failure as
unrelated without checking it.

When verification fails:

1. Identify the concrete failure.
2. Make the smallest appropriate fix.
3. Rerun the affected verification.
4. Rerun build and tests when the fix changed code.
5. Repeat until the change is green or genuine user input is required.

Never hide a known failure and declare completion. Failures that need
diagnosis go through `build-fix`.

| Situation | Workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Any implementation change, from first inspection to completion gates | `development-workflow` |
| Final verification before declaring work complete | `verify` |
| Code review or an independent second pass | `code-review` (agent: `code-reviewer`) |
| Failing build or tests to repair | `build-fix` |
| Adding, updating, or removing a NuGet/npm dependency | `add-dependency` |
| `CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md` value added, changed, or removed | `custom-settings` |
| New solution or project, or a repository-structure change | `project-structure` |
| Reserved decision or Decision Request | `architecture-decision` |
| Security audit or scan | `security-scan` |
| Any Git operation | `git-workflow` |
